programs.program: apazunersen / GTX-102, ASO suppressing UBE3A-AS to de-repress the silenced paternal UBE3A allele
programs.target: UBE3A-AS lncRNA (Angelman syndrome) — different gene, same mechanism class as our antagoNAT/allele-de-repression options and same 'relieve silencing of the intact allele' logic
programs.stage: Phase 3 Aspire (~129 patients) read out 2026-09-02: MISSED primary (Bayley-4 cognitive raw score) and key secondary (MDRI)
programs.key_result: Failed registrational trial despite earlier open-label developmental gains; the most mature clinical test of ASO-mediated de-repression of a silenced allele in a pediatric neurodevelopmental disorder
programs.changes_decision_because: Nearest-analogue allele-de-repression ASO failed Phase 3; raises endpoint, age-window and biomarker bar for CDD.

programs.stage: Phase 3 REVEAL ongoing (~200 participants), no Phase 3 readout found
programs.key_result: Still running after the competing GTX-102 Phase 3 failure; expressive communication chosen as primary endpoint rather than a cognitive raw score
programs.changes_decision_because: Endpoint choice, not mechanism, may have sunk Aspire; informs CDD outcome-measure selection before committing.

programs.program: zorevunersen (STK-001), TANGO ASO suppressing an SCN1A poison exon to raise productive SCN1A mRNA
programs.target: SCN1A non-productive splicing event (Dravet) — exactly the mechanism-1 payload class proposed for CDKL5, different gene
programs.delivery: Intrathecal, children 2 to <18; doses up to 70 mg; repeat dosing
programs.stage: Phase 3 EMPEROR fully enrolled (162 patients, Jun 2026); Phase 3 data expected Q3 2027; Phase 1/2a showed ~85% median seizure reduction at 3 months
programs.key_result: Only clinically advanced proof that poison-exon suppression can raise a haploinsufficient CNS gene; tolerability limited mainly to CSF protein elevation and procedural vomiting
programs.changes_decision_because: Validates chemistry, intrathecal pediatric dosing and safety envelope — payload potency is SCN1A-specific, not transferable to CDKL5.

programs.program: Published TANGO pipeline — Dravet and ADOA/OPA1 only
programs.target: SCN1A, OPA1; CDKL5 is NOT on the disclosed pipeline
programs.key_result: No CDKL5 TANGO program disclosed by the originator of the non-productive-splicing platform, despite CDD being a high-profile haploinsufficient CNS epilepsy
programs.changes_decision_because: Either CDKL5 lacks a usable non-productive event, or the lane is genuinely open — must resolve before committing.

programs.organization: UC Davis (Kyle Fink, Julian Halmai, David Cameron) — CIRM-funded, Loulou-affiliated
programs.program: Dual-effector split-dCas9 epigenome editing (transcriptional activation + DNA demethylation) at the CDKL5 promoter to reactivate the silenced allele
programs.target: CDKL5 locus itself on the inactive X — same gene, same tissue, same 'relieve X-silencing' biology as our XIST mechanism
programs.stage: Preclinical; preprint Aug 2025; dose-finding done, patient organoid validation done, manufacturing started, NHP toxicology beginning per 2025 CDKL5 Forum
programs.key_result: Restored CDKL5 protein and downstream signalling, rescued motor/cognitive deficits in Cdkl5 E6del heterozygous mice and normalised network activity in patient-derived NSCs and cortical organoids
programs.changes_decision_because: Proves locus-specific reactivation works and beats genome-wide XIST knockdown; makes XIST-ASO mechanism strategically obsolete.

programs.program: XIST-ASO plus DNA-demethylation combination to reactivate Xi-linked MECP2
programs.target: XIST RNA — the exact target of our mechanism-7, in a comparable X-linked neurodevelopmental disease
programs.delivery: Cell-based only; no in vivo CNS program or company program found
programs.stage: Preclinical/cellular; no clinical or disclosed industry program retrieved
programs.key_result: XIST ASO alone is insufficient — robust reactivation required co-inhibition of DNA methylation; reactivation is reversible on drug withdrawal and de-represses many X-linked genes
programs.changes_decision_because: Single-agent XIST ASO will not deliver CDKL5; combination requirement and off-gene de-repression kill the monotherapy case.

programs.organization: Elaaj Bio (wholly owned subsidiary of Loulou Foundation) with Viralgen (CDMO) and Jim Wilson/Penn
programs.target: CDKL5 — same gene, same tissue, mutation-agnostic
programs.stage: Manufacturing scale-up underway; CTA targeted ~end 2026; first clinical trial planned early 2027
programs.key_result: Disease foundation is funding and manufacturing its own AAV program; partnership announced 2026-05-05 with initial process development complete
programs.changes_decision_because: The key CDD foundation is committed to AAV first; an ASO program needs a differentiated niche and separate funding.

programs.program: UX055, AAV9 CDKL5 gene replacement with neuron-specific promoter
programs.target: CDKL5 — same gene, same CSF delivery route
programs.stage: Still preclinical as of 2025–26; IND filing publicly delayed beyond Q4 2023 and not yet filed; no discontinuation announcement found
programs.key_result: Multi-year IND slip for a well-resourced CDKL5 AAV program; supporting NHP expression work and mouse efficacy reported, but no clinical entry
programs.changes_decision_because: CDKL5 AAV dosing/expression control is evidently hard; a dose-titratable ASO has a real differentiation argument.

programs.program: CDKL5 AAV gene therapy (and all AAV gene therapy work)
programs.stage: DISCONTINUED; Biogen exited all AAV gene therapy work company-wide
programs.key_result: A third large-pharma CDKL5 AAV effort was terminated; EEG-in-mouse efficacy methodology was its main residual contribution
programs.changes_decision_because: Third AAV exit signals portfolio-level, not purely scientific, risk; EEG biomarker precedent is reusable for an ASO.

programs.organization: Chinese University of Hong Kong (Ip lab) et al.
programs.program: Adenine base editing correcting CDKL5 R550* in patient iPSC-derived neurons
programs.target: CDKL5 coding variant — same gene, variant-specific
programs.delivery: In vitro iPSC editing only; no in vivo CNS delivery demonstrated
programs.key_result: Restored CDKL5 protein and downstream signalling to isogenic-control levels and normalised neuronal morphology and transcriptome
programs.changes_decision_because: Sets the efficacy ceiling: endogenous-level, unaltered CDKL5. Our bounded-window upregulation must be benchmarked against it.
programs.source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-48097-y (direct fetch blocked by Nature IDP redirect; details from indexed abstract)

programs.organization: University of Ferrara / Italian academic groups
programs.program: Engineered U1 snRNA (ExSpeU1) rescue of CDKL5 splicing variants
programs.target: CDKL5 splice-region variants (e.g., partial intron retention, exon 16 skipping with c.2376+5G>A)
programs.stage: Published preclinical (IJMS 2019); no clinical follow-on found
programs.key_result: Confirms a real, mapped splice-defective CDKL5 patient subset with correctable aberrant splicing — the population where a splice-switching ASO is mechanistically strongest
programs.changes_decision_because: Defines a tractable splice-variant CDD subgroup — a competing modality already exists there, and an ASO alternative is credible.

programs.program: Individualized (n-of-1) CNS ASOs for nano-rare variants
programs.target: Mechanism- and gene-agnostic; splice-variant CDD patients are in scope
programs.delivery: Intrathecal, chronic, including pediatric; >3 years of continuous dosing in one patient
programs.key_result: No ASO-related serious adverse events across the treated cohort; FDA has specific guidance enabling this pathway
programs.changes_decision_because: Cheapest route to first-in-human CDKL5 ASO data via a splice-variant patient; gives chronic CNS safety precedent.

programs.program: Phase 1/2 open-label within-participant dose escalation of individualized ASOs for severe genetic CNS conditions
programs.target: Any variant amenable to ASO correction, age ≥1 year — CDKL5 splice variants eligible in principle
programs.key_result: A registered, multicentre regulatory framework for n-of-1 ASOs now exists, rather than ad hoc expanded access
programs.changes_decision_because: A ready clinical vehicle for a variant-specific CDKL5 ASO without building a standalone IND.

programs.target: 5-HT/5HT2C symptomatic seizure control — not CDKL5 RNA; defines the control arm
programs.stage: Positive Phase 3 (AES, Dec 2025); regulatory submission for CDD planned
programs.key_result: 47.6% vs 2.8% median reduction in countable motor seizures; 45.2% vs 4.5% ≥50% responders; CGI-I significant
programs.changes_decision_because: Standard of care is rising fast; a disease-modifying ASO cannot be positioned on seizure count alone.

programs.program: Bexicaserin (DEEp OCEAN Ph3) and relutrigine (EMERALD Ph3) in DEE/CDD
programs.target: 5HT2C agonism; next-generation sodium channel blockade — symptomatic comparators in the same patient population
programs.key_result: Two further Phase 3 symptomatic agents competing for the same small CDD trial population, with oral home dosing
programs.changes_decision_because: Enrolment competition plus oral convenience versus repeat intrathecal dosing weakens an ASO's recruitment and value case.

programs.program: Receptor-mediated BBB-crossing capsid for IV CNS delivery, flagged for future CDD use
programs.target: Delivery receptor at the BBB (capsid, not oligonucleotide conjugate)
programs.key_result: Active work to replace intrathecal CSF dosing with systemic BBB-crossing delivery for CDD specifically
programs.changes_decision_because: Signals the field expects CSF dosing to be superseded; non-intrathecal CNS exposure assumptions should be revisited.

programs.organization: Academic transcript annotation (Hector et al., PLoS ONE)
programs.program: Characterisation of CDKL5 transcript isoforms in human and mouse
programs.target: CDKL5 isoform architecture — prerequisite for every mechanism in our list
programs.key_result: hCDKL5_1 is the dominant CNS isoform: 9.7 kb, 18 exons, terminal exon 19, with a very large ~6.6 kb 3'UTR; exon 21 belongs to testis-restricted hCDKL5_5
programs.changes_decision_because: Resolves the flagged annotation gap: alternative-last-exon switching targets testis isoform, so the 6.6 kb 3'UTR is the real handle.

as_of: 2026-10-08 (most recent disclosure retrieved: Ultragenyx Phase 3 Aspire topline, 2026-09-02; Viralgen/Elaaj partnership, 2026-05-05)
